prompt: A company has earnings per share of $4.00, pays out 50% as dividends, has a required return of 12%, and sustainable growth rate of 6%. The justified leading P/E ratio is closest to:
explanation: The justified leading P/E = payout ratio / (r − g) = 0.50 / (0.12 − 0.06) = 0.50 / 0.06 = 8.33. This is derived from the Gordon Growth Model: P₀ = D₁/(r−g), and P₀/E₁ = (D₁/E₁)/(r−g) = payout ratio/(r−g). Option B (4.17) divides the payout ratio by r alone, ignoring growth: 0.50/0.12 = 4.17. Option C (12.50) uses 1/(r−g) without the payout adjustment: 1/0.08 = 12.50.
